Confirming the same panic on a new M5 MacBook Pro. It has happened twice, on July 29 and August 5.

Both times I was running a few active opencode sessions, maybe 2 or 3

Environment:

- OpenCode: `1.18.10`
- Install method: `Homebrew`
- macOS: 26.5.2 (`25F84`)
- Hardware: Apple M5 Pro macbook
- Terminal: `[iTerm & intelliJ terminal]`

Both panics had effectively the same signature:

```text
zone map exhausted while allocating from zone [data.kalloc.1024],
likely due to memory leak in zone [data.kalloc.1024]
```

July 29:

```text
data.kalloc.1024: 20G, 21258720 elements allocated
Panicked task: pid 46493: opencode.exe
Kernel extensions in backtrace:
  com.apple.iokit.EndpointSecurity
  com.apple.filesystems.apfs
```

August 5:

```text
data.kalloc.1024: 20G, 21259792 elements allocated
Panicked task: pid 25838: opencode.exe
Kernel extensions in backtrace:
  com.apple.iokit.EndpointSecurity
  com.apple.filesystems.apfs
```

This Mac also has active Endpoint Security system extensions from CyberArk EPM, Microsoft Defender, and Kandji. Those products do not appear by name in the panic backtrace - the backtrace only names Apple’s EndpointSecurity and APFS components - but the security stack may be a useful variable to compare.

I realize `opencode.exe` being the panicked task only tells us it made the allocation that finally exhausted the zone; it does not prove OpenCode created the underlying leak. However, seeing the same process and nearly identical allocation count in two separate panics seems worth adding to the existing reports.

Verified on Windows 11 x64 with Bun 1.3.14 and opencode-ai 1.18.8 installed globally.

The global Bun project package.json contained:

    "trustedDependencies": ["onnxruntime-node", "protobufjs"]

`bun pm untrusted` reported:

    .\\node_modules\\opencode-ai @1.18.8
     » [postinstall]: node ./postinstall.mjs

The package's `opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe` was a 479-byte text placeholder containing the message that the postinstall script was not run. Running the global `opencode` command then produced Bun's misleading error:

    Bun failed to remap this bin to its proper location within node_modules.

The actual platform binary worked directly:

    node_modules/opencode-windows-x64/bin/opencode.exe --version
    1.18.8

After placing that verified platform binary at the Bun global bin path, `opencode --version` and `opencode --help` worked, and `opencode serve` reached the `listening` state.

This appears to be the interaction between Bun's lifecycle-script trust policy and OpenCode's postinstall-based platform binary setup. A more actionable error could tell users to run `bun pm trust opencode-ai` (or install via npm/standalone) instead of reporting a corrupted node_modules remap.

The reproduction does not establish that a subagent was invoked. An `@lookup` mention instructs the primary agent to call the task tool, but the primary agent may answer directly instead. Corroborating this from the other side, via OpenCode Go (not the Zen free tier). Ran a 7-prompt probe against the `deepseek-v4-flash` route — mixed English/Chinese, leading and neutral phrasing, covering self-ID, architecture, and knowledge-recall boundary:

- Self-ID: "My model name is DeepSeek-V3, and my training data cutoff date is May 2025." In Chinese, explicitly: "DeepSeek V4 并不存在" (DeepSeek V4 does not exist).
- Asked cold for its own architecture, it reported 671B total / 37B active params, 128K context — the known V3-family signature, not V4-Flash-0731's published 284B total / 13B active, 1M-token context.
- Asked neutrally (no "V4" mentioned) for its most recent known DeepSeek release, it named DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, September 2025.

`/v1/models` on the Go gateway lists `deepseek-v4-flash` as a route and the key works, but the response carries no build/checkpoint metadata, so there's no way to verify from outside which weights are actually being served — seconding the ask in this thread for that to be added to the `/zen/go/v1/models` response. Happy to share the raw request/response pairs if useful for triage.

Correction to my comment above — ran the same 7-prompt battery against the official first-party DeepSeek API (`api.deepseek.com`, verified/paid key, `deepseek-v4-flash` confirmed as a listed model id) as a control, and it produces the same "V3-class" signature I flagged on Go: self-IDs as DeepSeek-V3/deepseek-chat, reports 671B/37B params (nearly word-for-word identical to the Go response), and even contradicts its own training-cutoff date across different calls (July 2024, May 2025, "mid-2024" in the same batch).

That means the architecture/cutoff numbers aren't a routing tell — they show up even where we're confident we're hitting the real, correctly-keyed endpoint. So I can no longer say this corroborates a Go-specific misrouting bug; what it actually shows is that self-report (identity, cutoff, and even specs) isn't a reliable signal for this model on *any* route, official or gateway. Retracting the "corroboration" framing — the original bug (no way to confirm which build is served without checkpoint metadata in `/v1/models`) still stands on its own, I just can't add weight to it with what I ran.

This is also a problem with Google GMail access. The following bug report was automatically created:

## Bug: `opencode mcp auth gmail` OAuth flow succeeds but token is not persisted

### Environment

- **opencode version**: 1.18.14
- **OS**: Linux
- **MCP server**: `gmail` (remote, Google MCP — `https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`)

### Config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`)

```json
"gmail": {
    "enabled": true,
    "type": "remote",
    "url": "https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1",
    "oauth": {
      "clientId": "XXXX",
      "clientSecret": "XXXX",
      "scope": "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.compose"
    }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `opencode mcp debug gmail` — shows `Auth status: ✗ not authenticated`
2. Run `opencode mcp auth gmail` — reports `Authentication successful!` and `Done`
3. Run `opencode mcp debug gmail` again — **still** shows `Auth status: ✗ not authenticated`
4. Any Gmail tool call (e.g. `gmail_search_threads`) returns `Unauthorized`
5. No OAuth tokens or credentials files appear in `~/.config/opencode/`

### Expected behavior

After `opencode mcp auth gmail` reports success, the OAuth token should be persisted so that:
- `opencode mcp debug gmail` reports `Auth status: ✓ authenticated`
- Gmail MCP tool calls succeed (e.g. `gmail_search_threads` returns data, not `Unauthorized`)

### Actual behavior

The OAuth flow completes successfully on the browser side, and opencode prints `Authentication successful!`, but no token is persisted. The auth state remains `not authenticated` and all tool calls are rejected with `Unauthorized`.

### Additional notes

- The server identifies as `StatelessServer` (debug output: `{"name":"StatelessServer","version":"ESF"}`), so it requires an auth token on every request — there is no session-level auth handshake.
- The connection itself succeeds (HTTP 200 OK from `https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`).
- Other remote MCP servers (e.g. `mcp-atlassian`) work correctly, so the issue is specific to the OAuth flow persistence.

Reproduced on OpenCode 1.18.14 for macOS arm64 with a Rust/schemars-based MCP server. The repeated AJV `console.warn()` messages were written into the TUI and visually corrupted it; `--log-level` did not suppress them.

A narrowly scoped local workaround now proxies only this MCP's JSON-RPC stream and recursively removes unsupported integer formats (`uint`, `uint8/16/32/64`, `int8/16/32/64`) only inside successful `result.tools` responses. It leaves non-tool messages byte-identical and preserves recognized formats.

Acceptance evidence:

- direct enumeration: 54 tools, 0 unsupported integer formats after normalization, 29 `double` formats preserved;
- three full OpenCode MCP enumerations: exit 0, 25 servers each, affected MCP connected;
- PTY TUI smoke: remained alive past startup, clean exit, no schema-warning flood.

This confirms the systemic client-side normalization approach requested here works without changing the MCP implementation or disabling schema validation.

Additional macOS arm64 evidence: OpenCode Desktop 1.18.10 produced the same uncaught async EPIPE path through `electron-log` console transport (`Socket._write` -> `console.info` -> `transport.writeFn`). Replacing it recoverably with the official signed/notarized 1.18.14 app yielded a detached hidden launch that remained alive for more than 10 minutes with no new EPIPE/uncaught/fatal/crash entry.

That is a non-reproduction result, not proof that 1.18.14 contains the fix: the 1.18.14 release predates merged PR #40794 and its notes do not mention EPIPE. The merged packaged-console change is the correct upstream resolution; a later release containing #40794 should remove the remaining uncertainty.

Adding +1 here — this is a **massive, recurring production blocker** for heavy OpenCode sessions (orchestrator + subagents, 150K+ context, long streaming responses).

**Observed frequency:** Multiple times per day under normal production use. The modal appears even when the full assistant response is already visible behind the dialog — the stream completed, but undici fires `terminated` on socket teardown, OpenCode classifies it as non-retryable `UnknownError`, and `halt()` kills the session despite a complete answer.

**Environment:**
- OpenCode 1.18.13
- CodeNomad GUI on Windows
- Local Docker OmniRoute gateway (SSE proxy to upstream LLM providers)
- API bridge keep-alive/header timeouts already raised to 65s/66s
- `OMNIROUTE_CHAT_MAX_HEAVY_IN_FLIGHT=8`

**Impact:**
- Entire session dies on a completed response — user loses all context, subagent state, and background task tracking
- No retry, no graceful degradation — just a modal and a dead session
- Windows-specific TCP handling in undici (Electron) makes this significantly worse than on Linux/macOS
- Workarounds (longer timeouts, fewer concurrent streams) reduce but do not eliminate the root cause

**Request:** This needs to be fixed in the next release. At minimum:
1. Classify `TypeError: terminated` as retryable in `MessageV2.fromError()` (alongside `ECONNRESET`) — PR #30638 proposed this but it was not merged
2. If the response body is already fully received, do NOT halt the session on a socket-teardown error — treat it as a benign transport close
3. Add a reconnect/resume path for interrupted SSE streams instead of hard-failing

This is not a rare edge case — it is the single most disruptive OpenCode bug for anyone running heavy agent workflows with a local gateway.

Adding +1 — this is a **severe, recurring production problem** that needs to ship a fix in the next release.

**Local diagnosis of the affected DB:**
- `opencode.db`: **4.71 GB**, 294,444 part rows, 71,439 messages, 2,485 sessions
- SQLite 3.50.4, WAL mode, `PRAGMA integrity_check` = `ok` (not corrupted)
- Disk free: 41.8 GB (no `SQLITE_FULL`)
- Largest part JSON blobs: ~5 MB each (step-finish snapshots with tool-call data)
- `part.id` is PRIMARY KEY (TEXT) — matches the `ON CONFLICT` target

**Observed behavior:**
- The error appears as a modal `Sitzungsfehler` (session error) in CodeNomad, killing the active session
- It frequently co-occurs with the `terminated` undici socket error (#30221): when the provider stream tears mid-response, the `PartUpdated` projector runs the upsert, and it fails — likely a **FK race** (PR #19526 addressed this for a related path but the `PartUpdated` projector in `projectors.ts` still only catches `foreign(err)`, rethrowing everything else)
- The error dialog does not include the SQLite error code, making root-cause isolation harder

**Root cause hypothesis (with evidence):**
1. **FK constraint race** — `part.message_id` references `message(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE; if the part write lands before the parent message commits, `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` fires and propagates uncaught
2. **Abort/lock contention** — an interrupted session holds a write lock; the projector's upsert conflicts
3. **Large payload + WAL checkpoint** — 5 MB JSON blobs in 294K rows with WAL checkpoint pressure

**What would help:**
1. Catch ALL DB errors in the `PartUpdated` projector (not just FK) — a failed part persistence should NEVER kill the session
2. Retry the upsert with backoff on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED
3. Consider pruning/compressing old part data, or adding a TTL/retention policy — 4.7 GB for session history is unsustainable
4. Include the SQLite error code in the failure message so users can distinguish FK race vs. constraint mismatch vs. locking

This is not a rare crash — it hits repeatedly during normal heavy agent workflows (orchestrator + subagents, long streaming responses). Please prioritize for the next release.

Thanks for the detailed report. We reviewed this against v1.18.10 and the current `dev` branch, but the evidence here does not indicate that context compaction is dropping MCP tool registrations.

The message `Your operational mode has changed from plan to build` is emitted when the session switches from the `plan` agent to the `build` agent; it is not a context-compaction message.

Also, `opencode debug agent build` reports the agent’s statically registered tools and their resolved permissions. It does not enumerate the MCP tools dynamically attached to a normal model request, so MCP tools being absent from that command’s output is expected and does not show that their registrations were lost. Normal session steps resolve connected MCP tools separately when constructing the request.

We’re closing this as not reproduced based on the current evidence. If the failure can be reproduced using an explicit compaction while remaining on the same agent, please open a new report with debug logs showing the MCP `listTools` result and the subsequent model request. That would let us distinguish an MCP server/proxy failure from tool filtering or request construction.

Cross-referencing related issues about the same root cause (web UI stops updating until a manual page refresh because the SSE event stream dies silently):

- #40502 — "Web interface does not auto-refresh conversations in real-time" (same symptom; received a detailed comment with the reverse-proxy/SSE analysis)
- #39352 — "Web UI freezes mid-session when the event stream dies silently; only a page refresh recovers" (identical symptom; identifies `server-sdk.tsx` reconnect logic and `session_status` drift)
- #39030 — "Mobile browser tab does not reconnect SSE stream after returning from another app" (same SSE reconnect gap, different trigger)
- #38458 — "SSE stream closes mid-turn (not persistent as documented)"
- #32175 — "SSE reconnection never fires after initial connection failure"

Summary of the common pattern: the web client's SSE consumer has no liveness check. When the `/global/event` connection dies without an error (proxy eviction, buffering stall, NAT/timeout), `reader.read()` never resolves, the reconnect loop never re-enters, and the UI stays frozen on the last rendered line until the user refreshes the page. Deployment-side (nginx `proxy_buffering off` for `text/event-stream`, keeping tunnels alive) mitigates, but the client should recover on its own.

Thanks for the trace — this matches what I'm seeing, and I verified the heartbeat/liveness question directly against the v1.18.14 source and a live probe.

## Environment (as requested)

- **OpenCode**: 1.18.14, `opencode web --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0 --cors https://opencode.afonsoft.dev` (systemd, basic auth `afonsoft`)
- **Browser**: Edge 151 (Chromium, `Chrome/151.0.0.0 ... Edg/151.0.0.0`) on Windows 11
- **Deployment**: Ubuntu 24.04 (aarch64) → nginx 1.30.2 (BT panel) reverse proxy on :80 → `proxy_pass http://localhost:4096` → opencode. Full chain: **browser → Cloudflare (Flexible SSL) → cloudflared tunnel → nginx → opencode:4096**
- **Who produces the new message**: the assistant. Sessions run server-side (provider `omniroute`, model `auto/best-coding`); all live updates (text deltas, tool calls, parts) arrive over the `/global/event` SSE stream. The messages that don't render are assistant-produced parts while the session keeps running.

## Heartbeat confirmation

**Server side (v1.18.14, from the bundle):** both `/global/event` and `/event` emit `server.connected` once, then `server.heartbeat` every **10 seconds** (Effect `$l("10 seconds")` schedule, `haltStrategy:"left"`). Headers: `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (so nginx buffering is disabled per-response), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `/global/event` is also excluded from the server's gzip middleware.

**Live probe through our nginx hop** (`curl -N` on `/global/event` via the proxy, 25s):
```
t=0.00s  server.connected
t=10.01s server.heartbeat
t=20.01s server.heartbeat   (connection still open when probe ended)
```
So heartbeats *do* keep flowing every 10s at the server/nginx level, with an open connection.

## Client side — this is the gap

`packages/app/src/context/server-sdk.tsx` (v1.18.14) confirms your finding:

- The consumer is a plain `for await (const event of events)` loop.
- Reconnect only happens when the loop **exits or throws**: `catch` → `finally` → `await wait(RECONNECT_DELAY_MS)` (=250ms) → next attempt.
- There is **no heartbeat-based liveness timeout anywhere**. The stream never yields a `server.heartbeat` to a timer; if the connection is open but silent (NAT/proxy/Cloudflare eviction without FIN/RST), `read()` never resolves, the loop never exits, and the UI stays frozen on the last rendered line until a manual refresh.

This is exactly the failure mode you described: a page refresh recreates the stream and reloads session data, which is why the symptom "runs fine, just doesn't show it".

## Extra evidence from nginx

`opencode.afonsoft.dev.error.log` recorded upstream drops on the stream:
```
upstream prematurely closed connection while reading upstream, request: "GET /global/event HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:4096/global/event"
```
So some drops do close at nginx level (those would be recovered by the 250ms reconnect), while the "stuck until refresh" cases are the ones that die without ever closing on a middle hop.

## Suggested fix direction

1. In `server-sdk.tsx`: add a liveness timer — if no SSE frame of any kind (heartbeats included) arrives within ~30s, `abort()` and let the reconnect loop restart the stream.
2. On reconnect, resync the affected session state (repair `session_status` / reload parts), otherwise a run that finished during the outage stays stale — same issue as #39352.
3. Proxy hygiene as mitigation: our nginx already passes heartbeats fine; Cloudflare/cloudflared keep-alives are configured. The client-side fix is the durable one.

Correlating: #39352, #39030, #38458, #32175 — same root cause, different triggers.

### Note on `.opencode/agent/orchestrator-agent-teams.md`

Quick clarification on the two pieces in this PR, since they can look coupled:

1. **The core feature is self-contained.** `Task(background=true)`, `next_agent`, and `agents_status` are core-native tools registered in the global builtin tool list (`packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts` — alongside `shell`, `read`, `task`, etc.). They are available to **every agent** in any session, with no config file required. The `next_agent`/`agents_status` implementations (`packages/opencode/src/tool/task-teams.ts`) contain no agent-name gating — they operate on background jobs filtered by session ID. Tests for both the registry wiring and the tools are included.

2. **The Agent-Teams file is an optional persona.** `agents/orchestrator-agent-teams.md` is just an agent definition (system prompt + `permission.task` allowlist) that makes a ready-made orchestrator agent available. It exists to demonstrate the workflow — it is **not required** for the primitives to function. Any developer or agent can use `Task(background=true)` + `next_agent` + `agents_status` directly.

So: the tools are the engine, the definition is a convenience wrapper. Happy to remove the `.opencode/agent/` file from this PR if you'd prefer it kept out, or to split it into a follow-up.

I traced this to source instead of guessing, and can answer the `证据？` ("evidence?") question above with code and reproducible tests.

## Where the error comes from

The string is thrown at exactly one place: `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/handler.ts`, inside `authenticate()` (current `dev`):

```ts
if (!data) throw new AuthError(t("zen.api.error.invalidApiKey"))
if (
  data.workspace.isBlocked ||
  (data.workspace.isFlaggedByAnthropic && modelInfo.id.startsWith("claude-")) ||
  (data.workspace.isFlaggedByOpenAI && modelInfo.id.startsWith("gpt-"))
)
  throw new AuthError(t("zen.api.error.requestBlockedByUpstreamProvider"))
```

Introduced in c40e3e74 ("zen: add security check", 2026-07-21 18:33 UTC) together with migration `20260721182121_wet_pestilence`, which adds the three workspace columns. First report of this string landed about two hours later (#38190).

**Which branch fires is forced by elimination.** The two vendor flags only apply to `claude-*` and `gpt-*` model ids. Everyone in this thread (me included) gets the error on `minimax-*`, `kimi-*`, `glm-*`, `deepseek-*`, `qwen*` — and even the `*-free` models. Only the `workspace.isBlocked` disjunct is model-agnostic. So affected accounts have `is_blocked = true` on their workspace row.

## Evidence it never reaches any upstream provider

1. **The anonymous inversion.** Byte-identical POSTs to `/zen/v1/chat/completions`, differing only in the `Authorization` header: `mimo-v2.5-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `longcat-2.0-free`, `deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `north-mini-code-free` all return **200 with a real completion anonymously** and **401 with my key** — in the same second. Anonymous requests return early in `authenticate()` (`if (!zenApiKey) { if (modelInfo.allowAnonymous) return ... }`) and never reach the flag check. The upstreams are demonstrably up, through this exact gateway.
2. **Latency.** Server-side time on the 401 is ~114 ms — the same as the purely local "Invalid API key." path, and far below any real relay round-trip. Nothing leaves the edge.
3. **Three distinct messages.** No header → "Missing API key."; garbage key → "Invalid API key."; real key → "Request blocked by upstream provider." Reaching the third message proves the key row exists and is not soft-deleted — so re-login, cache clearing, and key rotation (everything this thread has tried) cannot help.

## Why this thread has 30 comments and no diagnosis

The message says an upstream provider blocked the request. For the `is_blocked` branch no upstream was ever contacted — it is an opencode-side workspace block, surfaced with wording that points at a third party. That sends every affected user down the wrong debugging path (rotate key, clear cache, check billing, blame vendors).

Two asks:

1. **For the maintainers:** could someone check what `is_blocked` means operationally and what the remediation path is for accounts in this thread with active paid subscriptions? Several reporters (#38257, #39215) state their subscription is active and paid through dates in August. My own subscription was purchased directly on opencode.ai with my own card — if the flag came from the July 20 anti-reseller sweep, accounts like these are false positives, and #39827 shows recreating the account does not clear it.
2. **For the error message:** I've opened #40944, which splits `is_blocked` onto its own error string ("This workspace has been blocked. Contact support: …") so the next wave of affected users doesn't land here. Enforcement is unchanged — only the message.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #38351: Same root cause — permission glob patterns silently never match due to relative vs. absolute path mismatch in the permission matcher. That issue describes the inverse direction (runtime uses absolute paths but patterns are relative), while this issue describes absolute/`~` patterns failing against worktree-relative submitted paths. Both stem from the same path normalization gap in the permission matching pipeline.

I’d be wary of the “match both” fix. Since `evaluate()` is last-match-wins, running one target through two path namespaces leaves an awkward question: relative hits `allow`, absolute hits `deny` — which one gets to be “last”?

In BitFun we handle the target side at the tool boundary: turn it into one canonical absolute permission resource, then evaluate once. New files need the non-obvious bit: [canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor and append the missing tail](https://github.com/GCWing/BitFun/blob/e640aa402023792a5fd6568f445ece1a81013085/src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/restrictions.rs#L23-L58), otherwise `~/.ssh/new_key` falls straight through because it does not exist yet. I’d normalize configured globs into that same namespace and add the creation case to the regression alongside the two existing repros.
